prompt: Two triangular street signs have two pairs of congruent angles. Which criterion proves the signs are SIMILAR? Answer with two letters.
hint: Count what is known: two angles and no sides.

hints.text: Count what is known: two angles and no sides.
Two angles is enough for similarity, because the third angle comes free from the $180^\circ$ total.

explanation: If two angles of one triangle are congruent to two angles of another, the third pair must match too, since all three sum to $180^\circ$.
Matching angles means the same shape, though possibly a different size — that is similarity.

alternativeExplanations.title: Similar vs congruent
steps: Congruence needs at least one side, because sides set the size.
Similarity only cares about shape, so angles alone are enough — which is why AA works for similar but AAA fails for congruent.
